items.description: This 18th-century palace in Shaki served as the summer residence for the Khans. It is celebrated for its intricate wooden lattice work and vibrant stained glass.
Located in Nakhchivan, this 12th-century masterpiece is a prime example of the Nakhchivan architectural school. It is adorned with complex geometric patterns and Kufic calligraphy.
This unique two-story mausoleum is built directly into a steep cliff near Maraza. It dates back to the 15th century and remains a significant site of historical interest.
